title: Isolation, culture, and functional analysis of hepatocytes from mice with fatty liver disease
protocol: Prepare the perfusion buffer.
Place 40 mL of perfusion buffer in a 50 mL tube.
Heat the perfusion buffer to 42°C in a water bath for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare the digestion buffer.
Place 30 mL of digestion buffer in another 50 mL tube.
Heat the digestion buffer to 42°C in a separate section of the water bath for at least 30 minutes.
Set up the perfusion pump by mounting the peristaltic pump.
Immerse a long 1/32” ID × 3/32” OD silicone tubing in a water bath.
Connect the tubing to the pump using a 3/32” Polypropylene coupler.
Place the inlet tubing into a 50 mL tube with perfusion buffer in the 42°C water bath.
Set the peristaltic pump speed at 1–2 mL/min.
Assemble the outlet catheter by attaching a 25G 7/8 needle to the outlet tubing.
Rinse the pump with 10 mL of 70% EtOH followed by 10 mL of water.
Run the pump with perfusion buffer for 5 minutes to ensure an even flow rate.
Prepare the digestion buffer 1 hour prior to isolation and place it in a 42°C water bath.
Maintain buffers in a water bath at 42°C.
Euthanize the mouse by CO2 asphyxiation.
Clean the abdominal area with 70% EtOH.
Make an incision to expose the liver, inferior vena cava, and portal vein.
Place a catheter into the inferior vena cava.
Perfuse the liver using the maintained buffers at 42°C.
Digest the liver using collagenase IV solution.
Disassociate liver cells into a single-cell suspension.
Start the perfusion pump with perfusion buffer at a rate of 2 mL/min.
Ensure the correct flow rate by measuring the outlet volume as a fraction of time.
After 2 min, cut the hepatic portal vein to clear the liver from blood.
Continue the perfusion for an additional 10 min.
Add the digestion buffer to the 50 mL tube without stopping the pump when 2–5 mL is left of the perfusion buffer.
Digest for 10–20 min at 2 mL/min.
Carefully remove the liver including the gall bladder and place in a 10 cm petri dish kept on ice.
Add 10 mL cold plating medium to the dish.
Dissociate liver cells by gently swirling the liver in cold plating media without puncturing the gall bladder.
Generate a homogenous cell suspension using a pipette with a 1,000 μL tip.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 70 μm strainer placed on a 50 mL tube on ice.
Wash the plate with an additional 10 mL plating medium and transfer to the 50 mL tube.
Separate viable hepatocytes from dead hepatocytes and non-parenchymal cell types using Percoll gradient centrifugation.
Centrifuge the strained cells at 50 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–24°C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet in 20 mL of plating media.
Wash the cells twice by resuspending and centrifuging at 50 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the final pellet in 40 mL of plating media.
Divide the solution into four tubes, each containing 10 mL of solution.
Add 10 mL of 90% Percoll media to two tubes at 20°C–24°C.
Add 10 mL of 25% Percoll media to the remaining two tubes at 20°C–24°C.
Mix the solutions in each tube thoroughly.
Centrifuge one set of tubes containing 25% and 90% Percoll/hepatocytes at 100 × g.
Centrifuge another set of tubes containing 25% and 90% Percoll/hepatocytes at 1,000 × g.
Resuspend the pellets from both sets in 20 mL plating media.
Spin the resuspended samples at 50 × g for 4 min twice to remove Percoll media.
Resuspend the final hepatocyte pellets in 1 mL of medium.
Measure cell number and viability using trypan blue and a manual or automatic hemocytometer.
Seed cells into collagen-coated plates.
Plate 4 × 10^5 viable cells in 6-well plates or 2 × 10^5 cells in 12-well plates.
Place the plated cells in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2 for 3–4 hours.
Wash the plated cells once with PBS to remove dead cells after 3–4 hours.
Replace the medium with maintenance medium.
Start experiments on the same or next day.
Prepare 7 mL oil red O solution by mixing oil red O with H2O at a 3:2 ratio.
Gently wash cells twice with 1 mL PBS.
Add 0.5 mL per well of 3% Formalin diluted in PBS and incubate for 0.5–1 h at 20°C–24°C.
Discard the formalin and wash cells twice with 1 mL ddH2O.
Add 0.5 mL 60% isopropanol and incubate for 5 min.
Discard the isopropanol and apply oil red O working solution.
Rotate the plate to ensure even distribution and incubate for 10–20 min at 20°C–24°C.
Discard the oil red O solution and wash cells 2–5 times with ddH2O until clear.
Add 1 mL ddH2O and view red lipid droplets under a microscope using a 40× objective.
Optional: Add Hematoxylin after step 36 and incubate for 1 minute.
After discarding Hematoxylin, wash cells 2–5 times with ddH2O until clear.
Critical: Do not store the mixed oil red O solution for more than 2 h.
